Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model Simulation using YUIMA

Source: R/dns-simulation.r
simulate_dns_factors.Rd

Functions to simulate yield curves using the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel model with YUIMA package for SDE simulation.

Simulates the evolution of DNS factors using a multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process implemented with the YUIMA package for accurate stochastic differential equation simulation.

Usage

simulate_dns_factors(
  params,
  initial_factors,
  time_horizon = 10,
  n_steps = 120,
  n_paths = 100,
  include_correlation = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  sim_method = "euler",
  engine = c("yuima", "exact")
)

Arguments

params

List. Model parameters (kappa, theta, sigma).

initial_factors

Numeric vector. Initial factor values (beta1, beta2, beta3).

time_horizon

Numeric. Simulation time horizon in years.

n_steps

Integer. Number of time steps in the simulation.

n_paths

Integer. Number of simulation paths.

include_correlation

Logical. Whether to include correlations in simulations.

seed

Integer. Random seed for reproducibility.

sim_method

Character. Discretisation scheme passed to YUIMA, either "euler" (the default) or "milstein". Ignored by engine = "exact", which does not discretise.

engine

Character. "yuima" (the default) simulates through the YUIMA package, one call per path. "exact" samples the exact Gaussian transition law of the factor system directly: it needs no extra package, carries no discretisation error at any step size, and is roughly two orders of magnitude faster. The default is expected to change to "exact" in a future release.

Value

A list containing:

  • factors: Array of simulated factors (time, path, factor)

  • time: Vector of time points

  • params: The input parameters

  • sim_method: The scheme used

  • engine: The engine used

Details

The simulation is based on the multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process: $$d\beta(t) = \kappa(\theta - \beta(t))dt + \sigma dW(t)$$ where \(\kappa\) is the mean-reversion matrix, \(\theta\) is the long-run mean vector, \(\sigma\) is the volatility matrix, and \(W(t)\) is a correlated Wiener process.

This implementation uses the YUIMA package, which provides efficient and accurate methods for simulating stochastic differential equations.

The diffusion coefficient of this model does not depend on the state, so the Milstein correction term vanishes and sim_method = "milstein" coincides with the Euler-Maruyama scheme. The argument is honoured for completeness; accuracy is governed by n_steps.

That accuracy ceiling is what engine = "exact" removes. The factor system is a linear SDE with state-independent diffusion, so its transition density over any step is Gaussian with a mean and covariance available in closed form. Sampling that law directly is exact in distribution at every step size, and replaces one YUIMA call per path with vectorised draws over all paths at once. The two engines agree in distribution; they do not produce the same paths from the same seed.

Examples

params <- list(
  kappa = c(0.02, 0.3, 0.5),
  theta = c(0.04, -0.02, 0.01),
  sigma = c(0.005, 0.01, 0.02),
  correlation = diag(3)
)
initial_factors <- c(0.035, -0.015, 0.005)

# The exact engine needs no extra package
sim_result <- simulate_dns_factors(params, initial_factors, n_paths = 50,
                                   engine = "exact", seed = 1)
sim_result
#> DNS simulation
#>   50 paths, 120 steps over 10 years
#>   engine           exact
#>   terminal factors 0.0353  -0.0181  0.0107
#>     (sd)           0.0152  0.0143  0.0193

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# The YUIMA engine, for comparison
simulate_dns_factors(params, initial_factors, n_paths = 50, engine = "yuima")
} # }
